homePage.heroSubtitle: Calculate and convert aspect ratios for social media, video, photography and screens
homePage.whatIsAspectRatioText: An aspect ratio describes the proportional relationship between width and height. Written as W:H (e.g., 16:9), it tells you the shape of a screen, image, or video frame. A 16:9 ratio means for every 16 units of width, the height is 9 units — the standard for HD and 4K video. A 1:1 ratio is a perfect square, used for Instagram feed posts.
homePage.howToUseStep1Text: Enter your original dimensions (the ratio locks automatically), then type a new width or height — the other dimension calculates instantly. Pick a platform preset to auto-fill recommended dimensions.
homePage.howToUseStep2Text: Enter any width and height to discover the simplified ratio, decimal value, closest standard match, and CSS padding-bottom value. Upload an image to instantly detect its dimensions.
homePage.howToUseStep3Text: Upload any image and choose where you want to use it — social media, websites, print, or personal use. Get instant recommendations with crop analysis and one-click dimension copying.

aboutPage.title: About
aboutPage.heading: About the Aspect Ratio Calculator
aboutPage.lead: A free tool for working out aspect ratios and resizing to them without guesswork. No account, no upload, no cost.
aboutPage.purpose: Aspect ratio sits underneath a lot of work that is not about aspect ratio. A photograph that needs cropping. A slide that has to fill a projector. A television bought for the kind of films you actually watch. A container that needs an exact height in code. In every one of those the decision is the same small piece of arithmetic, and getting it wrong shows immediately: something is too big, too small, soft, or surrounded by space that should not be there. Some of that you can fix by eye. Code you cannot — it wants a number. This site exists to make that decision quickly and then get out of the way.
aboutPage.whatItDoes: Three things. The calculator resizes a width or a height while holding a ratio fixed. Find-ratio takes any two dimensions and tells you the ratio they make, reduced to its simplest form. The Image Wizard takes an image, reads its dimensions automatically, and shows how it will crop on each major social platform.
aboutPage.privacy: Every calculation runs in your browser. Images opened in the Image Wizard are read locally and are never uploaded, stored or transmitted — there is no server to send them to. The site also installs as an app and keeps working with no connection at all.
aboutPage.languages: The calculator, the guides and the platform reference pages are published in English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Indonesian, Japanese, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Arabic, Ukrainian, Polish, Romanian and Vietnamese.
aboutPage.maintenance: Social platform dimensions change, so the platform pages are reviewed against each platform's own published specification rather than copied from other guides. Every article carries the date it was published, and that date is only moved when the words actually change.
aboutPage.contactCta: Found something wrong, or something missing?

contactPage.title: Contact
contactPage.heading: Contact
contactPage.lead: Corrections, feature requests and bug reports are all welcome, and all read.
contactPage.feedback: The feedback form is the fastest route. It takes a message and, optionally, what you use the calculator for — which is what decides what gets built next.
contactPage.security: Security reports follow RFC 9116. The machine-readable contact details are published at /.well-known/security.txt, and reports sent through the feedback form reach the same place.
contactPage.data: Nothing you calculate is transmitted, so there is nothing to request or delete. What the site does collect, and how to turn it off, is set out in the privacy policy.

developersPage.title: API
developersPage.heading: Developer API
developersPage.lead: The calculator is callable. No key, no account, no rate limit beyond ordinary fair use — and every response says where it came from.
developersPage.ratio: Give it a width and a height and it returns the simplified ratio. Give it a ratio and one dimension and it returns the other. Give it nothing and it lists every named ratio on the site.
developersPage.content: Every content page has a JSON representation of the same resource. You can request it directly, or ask for it on the page's own URL by sending an Accept header of application/json — the HTML and the JSON are the same thing in two forms.
developersPage.spec: The full OpenAPI 3.1 description of both endpoints, so a client can be generated rather than written.
developersPage.cors: Cross-origin requests are allowed from anywhere. The responses are public arithmetic over public data — there is no session and nothing here that is not already on the page.
developersPage.terms: Free to use, including commercially, with attribution to aspect-ratio-calculator.com. If the API saves you building your own, a link back is the whole price.

safeZoneTool.title: Instagram Reels Safe Zone Checker — Free
safeZoneTool.description: Check what Instagram Reels, TikTok and YouTube Shorts cover on your 1080 × 1920 frame — and how much width the phone screen itself cuts off.
safeZoneTool.h1: Safe zone checker for Reels, TikTok and Shorts
safeZoneTool.answer: A safe zone is the part of a 1080 × 1920 frame that nothing covers. Instagram Reels, TikTok and YouTube Shorts each reserve different margins for captions, buttons and the profile bar. There is a second loss almost nobody accounts for: modern phone screens are taller than 9:16, so a correctly sized Reel is scaled up to fill the screen and roughly 18% of its width is pushed off the edges — about 97 pixels per side on an iPhone 15. No export setting changes that; you frame for it.
safeZoneTool.fact1: The canvas is the same 1080 × 1920 on all three platforms. What differs is how much of it the app paints over.
safeZoneTool.fact2: The screen crop is arithmetic, not opinion: a 9:16 video is 1.78 times taller than wide, an iPhone 15 screen is 2.17, and filling the screen top to bottom pushes the difference off the sides.
safeZoneTool.fact3: On a genuine 9:16 screen the crop is exactly zero, which is the check that the formula is right.
safeZoneTool.showCrop: Show the screen crop on the frame
safeZoneTool.frameAlt: Safe area on a {w} by {h} frame
safeZoneTool.screenDominates: On this phone the screen takes more width than the interface does. Designing to the published safe zone alone would still lose {px} px a side.
safeZoneTool.provenanceOurs: The screen crop is computed here from each phone's published resolution — you can check it: scale 1080 × 1920 until its height matches the screen, and whatever the width exceeds the screen by is what you lose. A true 9:16 screen returns zero, which is the test that the formula is right.
safeZoneTool.provenanceNotOurs: The interface margins are not ours.
safeZoneTool.provenanceUnverified: , and not yet verified against a current build by us
safeZoneTool.provenanceMoves: Platforms move these without announcing it, so treat them as a guide and the arithmetic as the guarantee.
safeZoneTool.reelsTop: status bar and the Reels/Following switcher
safeZoneTool.reelsBottom: username, caption, audio ticker and the progress bar
safeZoneTool.reelsSides: the like / comment / share / audio rail down the right
safeZoneTool.reelsSource: ARC's own platform copy, which states a 1080×1420 centred safe area with 250px reserved top and bottom. Side figures are the conventional values for the action rail and have not been measured here.
safeZoneTool.tiktokBottom: username, caption, music title — TikTok's caption block is the deepest of the three and it grows with the caption
safeZoneTool.tiktokSides: avatar, like, comment, bookmark, share and the spinning record
safeZoneTool.tiktokSource: Conventional published values; not measured against a build here.
safeZoneTool.shortsBottom: channel name, title, and the Subscribe button
safeZoneTool.shortsSides: like, dislike, comments, share, remix and the sound disc
safeZoneTool.shortsSource: Conventional published values; not measured against a build here.
